study type: Observational study using a national population-based database
cohort: Nulliparous women with term, singleton, vertex pregnancies from Black and White patients in the Nationwide Inpatient Sample database (2008-2011)
finding: Within-hospital disparities in cesarean delivery rates were lower in minority-serving hospitals, rural hospitals, and the South compared to their respective counterparts.
mod_finding: Black women are more likely to have a cesarean delivery than White women, and these disparities vary across hospitals depending on factors such as minority-serving status, location, and region.
